# Sentiment Analysis

## Approach

The project replicates and builds on the sentiment analysis example from Chapter 2 of Text Mining with R: A Tidy Approach by Julia Silge and David Robinson. The chapter uses text scoring by looking up each word in a sentiment dictionary and summing the results. It exemplifies this by scoring the novels of Jane Austen using the AFINN, Bing, and NRC dictionaries.

In the first part of the project, I will replicate the code from the book in a Quarto document, referencing the book and the source. This includes loading the dictionaries, tidying the novels into one-word-per-row format, scoring sentiment throughout each novel in 80-line chunks, comparing all three dictionaries for Pride and Prejudice, identifying the most positive and negative words, creating word clouds, and the most negative chapters in each novel.

Secondly, I will replace the current corpus with US State of the Union addresses, from the sotu package, as well as add the Syuzhet lexicon, from the syuzhet package, making a total of four lexicons. Because speeches do not have chapters or lines, I will score by year rather than by 80-line intervals, normalized for 1,000 words to control for variations in speech length. I will perform comparisons between the four lexicons using trajectories, correlation, lexicon coverage, and the most impactful words, and interpret the results in the context of the Austen example, including the impact of the new domain and scoring one word at a time

## Code Base

### Reproducing Chapter 2 Example

```{r}
library(tidytext)
library(janeaustenr)
library(dplyr)
library(stringr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(wordcloud)
library(reshape2)
library(purrr)
```

```{r}
install.packages("textdata")
```

```{r}
get_sentiments("afinn")
```

```{r}
get_sentiments("bing")
```

```{r}
get_sentiments("nrc")
```

```{r}
tidy_books <- austen_books() %>%
  group_by(book) %>%
  mutate(
    linenumber = row_number(),
    chapter = cumsum(str_detect(text,
                                regex("^chapter [\\divxlc]",
                                      ignore_case = TRUE)))) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  unnest_tokens(word, text)
```

```{r}
nrc_joy <- get_sentiments("nrc") %>%
  filter(sentiment == "joy")

tidy_books %>%
  filter(book == "Emma") %>%
  inner_join(nrc_joy) %>%
  count(word, sort = TRUE)
```

```{r}
jane_austen_sentiment <- tidy_books %>%
  inner_join(get_sentiments("bing")) %>%
  count(book, index = linenumber %/% 80, sentiment) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = sentiment, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) %>%
  mutate(sentiment = positive - negative)
```

```{r}
ggplot(jane_austen_sentiment, aes(index, sentiment, fill = book)) +
  geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~book, ncol = 2, scales = "free_x")
```

```{r}
pride_prejudice <- tidy_books %>% 
  filter(book == "Pride & Prejudice")

pride_prejudice
```

```{r}
afinn <- pride_prejudice %>% 
  inner_join(get_sentiments("afinn")) %>% 
  group_by(index = linenumber %/% 80) %>% 
  summarise(sentiment = sum(value)) %>% 
  mutate(method = "AFINN")

bing_and_nrc <- bind_rows(
  pride_prejudice %>% 
    inner_join(get_sentiments("bing")) %>%
    mutate(method = "Bing et al."),
  pride_prejudice %>% 
    inner_join(get_sentiments("nrc") %>% 
                 filter(sentiment %in% c("positive", 
                                         "negative"))
    ) %>%
    mutate(method = "NRC")) %>%
  count(method, index = linenumber %/% 80, sentiment) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = sentiment,
              values_from = n,
              values_fill = 0) %>% 
  mutate(sentiment = positive - negative)
```

```{r}
bind_rows(afinn, 
          bing_and_nrc) %>%
  ggplot(aes(index, sentiment, fill = method)) +
  geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~method, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y")
```

```{r}
get_sentiments("nrc") %>% 
  filter(sentiment %in% c("positive", "negative")) %>%
```

```{r}
p_and_p_sentences <- tibble(text = prideprejudice) %>% 
  unnest_tokens(sentence, text, token = "sentences")

p_and_p_sentences$sentence[2]
```

```{r}
austen_chapters <- austen_books() %>%
  group_by(book) %>%
  unnest_tokens(chapter, text, token = "regex", 
                pattern = "Chapter|CHAPTER [\\dIVXLC]") %>%
  ungroup()

austen_chapters %>% 
  group_by(book) %>% 
  summarise(chapters = n())
```

```{r}
bingnegative <- get_sentiments("bing") %>% 
  filter(sentiment == "negative")

wordcounts <- tidy_books %>%
  group_by(book, chapter) %>%
  summarize(words = n())

tidy_books %>%
  semi_join(bingnegative) %>%
  group_by(book, chapter) %>%
  summarize(negativewords = n()) %>%
  left_join(wordcounts, by = c("book", "chapter")) %>%
  mutate(ratio = negativewords/words) %>%
  filter(chapter != 0) %>%
  slice_max(ratio, n = 1) %>% 
  ungroup()
```

### Extending Analysis

The sotu package contains the text of the U.S. President's State of the Union address along with metadata, with sotu_meta containing president, year, party and type of speech. The text spans over two centuries. There is no text to break into chapters/lines so the unit of text will be per year.

```{r}
library(sotu)

sotu_df <- sotu_meta %>%
  mutate(text = sotu_text) %>%
  select(president, year, party, text)

sotu_tidy <- sotu_df %>%
  unnest_tokens(word, text)

total_words <- sotu_tidy %>% count(year, name = "total_words")

glimpse(sotu_df)
nrow(sotu_tidy)
```

The Syuzhet dictionary was created by Matthew Jockers in the Nebraska Literary Lab, using human coded sentence level data in a corpus of fiction. It can be accessed through the syuzhet R package. Unlike the AFINN word list it is a numerical list, with values ranging from approximately -1 to 1.

```{r}
library(syuzhet)

syuzhet_lex <- get_sentiment_dictionary("syuzhet") %>%
  as_tibble() %>%
  select(word, value)

afinn_lex <- get_sentiments("afinn")
bing_lex  <- get_sentiments("bing")
nrc_lex   <- get_sentiments("nrc") %>%
  filter(sentiment %in% c("positive", "negative"))

range(syuzhet_lex$value)
nrow(syuzhet_lex)
```

Speeches differ a lot in length, so unlike Austen's fixed 80-line sections, raw sums would mostly track how long each address was. To balance this, I will divide each year's net score by its total word count and express it per 1,000 words.

```{r}
score_numeric <- function(lex, method) {
  sotu_tidy %>%
    inner_join(lex, by = "word") %>%
    group_by(year) %>%
    summarise(raw = sum(value)) %>%
    mutate(method = method)
}
```

```{r}
score_binary <- function(lex, method) {
  sotu_tidy %>%
    inner_join(lex, by = "word") %>%
    count(year, sentiment) %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = sentiment, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) %>%
    mutate(raw = positive - negative) %>%
    select(year, raw) %>%
    mutate(method = method)
}
```

```{r}
sotu_scores <- bind_rows(
  score_numeric(afinn_lex, "AFINN"),
  score_binary(bing_lex, "Bing et al."),
  score_binary(nrc_lex, "NRC"),
  score_numeric(syuzhet_lex, "Syuzhet")
) %>%
  left_join(total_words, by = "year") %>%
  mutate(score = raw / total_words * 1000) %>%
  group_by(method) %>%
  mutate(z = as.numeric(scale(score))) %>%
  ungroup()
```

```{r}
ggplot(sotu_scores, aes(year, score, fill = method)) +
  geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~method, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Net sentiment per 1,000 words")
```
